Diazonium salts have the general structure R-N≡N+ X-, where R is typically an aromatic group and X- is an anion like Cl-. They are important intermediates in organic synthesis.

When diazonium salts undergo reactions such as:
1. Sandmeyer reactions (replacement of the diazonium group with halides)
2. Replacement with hydroxyl groups
3. Reduction to form arenes
4. Coupling reactions with aromatic compounds

In all these reactions, the diazonium group (N≡N+) is lost from the molecule and forms nitrogen gas (N₂) as a byproduct. This is one of the driving forces of these reactions, as the formation of the stable N₂ molecule is thermodynamically favorable.

The evolution of nitrogen gas is actually a characteristic feature of diazonium salt reactions and is often used as evidence that the reaction is proceeding as expected.
